jobs.title: Integrated Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT POINTFIVE

PointFive finds the cost buried inside enterprise infrastructure, from the cloud to coding agents. We pioneered DeepWaste across cloud and data platforms, and we are now doing the same for AI token spend with TokenShift. 
Fanatics, H&M, Hertz, Nubank, Citizens Bank and other Fortune 500 companies use PointFive to see and cut what their infrastructure and AI actually cost.

We have raised $96 million, most recently a $60 million Series B led by Accel https://www.pointfive.co/press/pointfive-raises-60m-series-b. Engineering sits in Tel Aviv and our go-to-market team is focused on North America. PointFive Labs, our research arm, publishes original work on how infrastructure and AI actually get paid for.

CRN named us one of the 10 hottest cloud computing startups of 2026 https://www.crn.com/news/cloud/2026/the-10-hottest-cloud-computing-startups-of-2026-so-far?page=9, Forbes Israel put us on its Next Billion Dollar Startups list https://forbes.co.il/rankings/2025nextbilliondollarstartups/, and Redpoint selected us for its InfraRed 100 https://www.pointfive.co/press/pointfive-infrared-100, its ranking of the private companies shaping the future of cloud infrastructure.


ABOUT THE ROLE

This is the connective tissue of our marketing. Product marketing, content, field, PR, partners, web and our outside agencies each own their piece. You make sure the pieces fit: that everyone knows what's coming, what they owe, and when, so we all move together.

You won't write every word, run every event or own every relationship. You will see the dependencies nobody else sees, bring the right people together early, and keep everyone accountable to the dates, including very senior people. It takes real experience to do this well, and the judgment to know when to push and when to adjust.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Keep one shared view of everything marketing has coming, months ahead, so every team plans against the same picture.

 - Think strategically about sequence. Decide what should come first, what builds on it and what lands last, so each launch, story, event and partner moment sets up the next one instead of competing with it.

 - Work backwards from the big moments on the calendar and map the interdependencies: what has to be true, by when, for each one to land.

 - Spot the connections early: which launch, story, event, partner and customer moment belong together.

 - Bring the right people into the room at the right time and make sure each knows what they own and when it's due.

 - Run the rhythm that keeps marketing, product, sales and partnerships in sync week to week.

 - Make sure the website and our other channels reflect what we're saying, working with the people who own them.

 - Give our agencies and outside partners clear direction so their work lands right the first time.

 - Notice when something is slipping before anyone else does, and fix it or flag it.


THE KIND OF SITUATIONS YOU'LL HANDLE

 - A major conference is four months out. Work backwards so that the product news, the story behind it, the press, the partners and the customer voices are all ready at the right moment, and every owner knows it.

 - Three teams are planning three good ideas for the same month. Turn them into one moment instead of three competing ones.

 - A launch date moves. Figure out everything downstream that moves with it, and get everyone re-aligned before it becomes a problem.

 - A partner wants to do something together. Make sure it fits the bigger plan and doesn't collide with what's already coming.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

You probably haven't had this exact title. The people who do this well usually took a winding path through events, content, product marketing, community, sales, producing or founding something. What they share is that they make things happen.

 - You have real, hands-on marketing experience, ideally in B2B tech, across more than one discipline.

 - You have built something from scratch: a community, an event, a program, a side project, something nobody asked you to start.

 - You have kept many moving parts and many people on track at once, and you have the stories to prove it.

 - You think in plans, calendars and dependencies. Things don't fall through the cracks around you.

 - You have ideas and you see them through. Landing six moving parts in the right order is your idea of a good week.

 - You solve problems sideways when the budget, the time or a missing piece gets in the way.

 - You're hungry. Your scope keeps growing because you pick up what nobody owns.

 - You hold people accountable, kindly, including people more senior than you.

 - You write clearly in English and Hebrew and can brief anyone so they get it right the first time.




WHAT DOESN'T MATTER, AND WHAT'S A BONUS

Doesn't matter: your current title, a specific number of years, a marketing degree, or whether you have held a role like this before. You don't need to code.

Bonus points:

 - You have built things with AI tools (workflows, agents, automations) that made you or your team faster.

 - You have worked with cloud or AI infrastructure buyers, or alongside hyperscaler and partner teams.

 - You have run a launch, an event or a program end to end, from blank page to results.

 - You have worked at both an early-stage startup and a company that was scaling fast.

You don't need to tick every box. Show us you can really own this.




YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Days 1 to 30: You know every team, partner and vendor we work with. You have mapped what's planned, what's in flight and what's missing, and you've shipped at least one thing yourself.

 - Days 31 to 60: One shared view of what's coming is live, and every team plans against it. A weekly rhythm is running. The next major moment is mapped backwards, with every owner and date agreed.

 - Days 61 to 90: You've coordinated a connected moment from start to finish: launch, content, PR, partner and event pulling in the same direction. Other teams now come to you first.


HOW WE'LL KNOW IT'S WORKING

 - Big moments land on time, with every piece pointing the same way.

 - Every team plans against the same picture of what's coming.

 - Agencies and partners deliver better work because the direction is clearer.

 - People across the company come to you first to find out what's happening and where they fit.


WHAT YOU MIGHT NOT LOVE

 - A lot of your job is chasing people who are busy, some of them very senior.

 - Plans change often. You'll rework the picture more than once a quarter and still keep everyone aligned.

 - Much of your best work is invisible when it goes well. The moment lands, and it looks easy.

 


WHY POINTFIVE

 - Founders with a track record — Built and sold IntSights to Rapid7. Backed by top-tier investors with deep conviction in this category.

 - Category-defining product — DeepWaste detection and agentic remediation with clear, measurable ROI for both engineering and finance teams.

 - Early-stage leverage — Your work directly shapes the product, the culture, and the go-to-market playbook.

 - Your role has a view across the whole company —  product, research, partners, sales and leadership all run through this seat. Direct access to founders and leadership, and room to act without layers of approval.

jobs.title: Creative Growth Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT POINTFIVE

PointFive finds the cost buried inside enterprise infrastructure, from the cloud to coding agents. We pioneered DeepWaste across cloud and data platforms, and we are now doing the same for AI token spend with TokenShift. 
Fanatics, H&M, Hertz, Nubank, Citizens Bank and other Fortune 500 companies use PointFive to see and cut what their infrastructure and AI actually cost.

We have raised $96 million, most recently a $60 million Series B led by Accel https://www.pointfive.co/press/pointfive-raises-60m-series-b. Engineering sits in Tel Aviv and our go-to-market team is focused on North America. PointFive Labs, our research arm, publishes original work on how infrastructure and AI actually get paid for.

CRN named us one of the 10 hottest cloud computing startups of 2026 https://www.crn.com/news/cloud/2026/the-10-hottest-cloud-computing-startups-of-2026-so-far?page=9, Forbes Israel put us on its Next Billion Dollar Startups list https://forbes.co.il/rankings/2025nextbilliondollarstartups/, and Redpoint selected us for its InfraRed 100 https://www.pointfive.co/press/pointfive-infrared-100, its ranking of the private companies shaping the future of cloud infrastructure.


ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a hands-on creative role. You will come up with ideas, build them, ship them and watch what happens. The goal is buzz, shares, followers, mindshare and category authority. Pipeline follows attention, but attention is the job.

You will take rough concepts from our leadership and turn them into real campaigns on your own, and you will bring plenty of your own. You will think about distribution while you are still shaping the idea, not after it is finished.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Invent and ship campaigns, games, competitions, tools, lists, stunts, videos and interactive experiences that people choose to share.

 - Turn PointFive's research into stories that engineers, executives and press repeat.

 - Make customers, practitioners and partners the heroes of the story, so they are proud to share it with their own networks.

 - Get our people, customers and community sharing our work because they want to.

 - Give PointFive a distinctive personality and voice across LinkedIn, Reddit, communities and events.

 - Support the creative themes for our conferences and events, and tie them into bigger campaigns, working alongside our field marketing team who bring them to life.

 - Make PointFive the name people think of, and the source they reach for, when the topic is infrastructure and AI cost.

 - Run lots of fast experiments, keep what works and drop what doesn't without drama.


THE KIND OF BRIEFS YOU'LL GET

 - Take a dry enterprise number and turn it into something people argue about in the comments.

 - A customer just saved a lot of money. Make them the hero of something they actually want to post.

 - A big industry conference is one moment in a three-month campaign. Give the whole thing a theme people remember, and make ours the booth they talk about after they leave.

 - Build something interactive, a tool, a game or a quiz, that people send to their team.

 - Our category all looks and sounds the same. Show us something that doesn't.


YOU MIGHT BE THE PERSON IF

 - You have built an audience from zero yourself. A newsletter, a following, a community, a side project, a meetup. You know what it takes to go from 10 people to 10,000 without a famous logo behind you.

 - You are extremely online. You understand LinkedIn, Reddit, communities, memes and how things spread, and you use them yourself.

 - You have made things people voluntarily shared, and you can point to them.

 - You write very well and you are funny on purpose.

 - You can make a technical or "boring" enterprise category interesting to technical buyers.

 - You have done the work yourself, not only briefed agencies.

 - You are comfortable with a lot of your experiments failing.

 - You are hungry to make breakout work you can put your name on.

You don't need every one of these. Show us you can own this.



BONUS POINTS IF YOU

 - Can code or vibecode well enough to ship a landing page, a leaderboard or a small tool without waiting for engineering.

 - Have a portfolio of experiments, including the ones that flopped.

 - Have worked somewhere early during a breakout moment and can say exactly what you contributed.

 - Know cloud, FinOps, dev tools or AI infrastructure, or are curious enough to learn it fast.


THIS PROBABLY ISN'T FOR YOU IF

 - You want to run a content calendar, manage a social inbox or optimize lead forms.

 - You mostly manage agencies and teams rather than make things yourself.


WHAT YOU MIGHT NOT LOVE

 - You are the first person doing this at PointFive. There is no playbook, no asset library and no creative team underneath you.

 - Making a customer or partner the hero means getting their comms team to say yes. Some great ideas will die in someone else's legal review.

 - A lot of your experiments will fail in public.

 - Your manager is a pop culture addict who will bother you with ideas only he finds funny. You are allowed, and expected, to say "no, that's ridiculous." If you can't enjoy a ridiculous idea even when you kill it, don't join.


HOW WE'LL KNOW IT'S WORKING

 - More people follow, share and talk about PointFive and our leaders, month over month.

 - PointFive becomes the name people bring up first when the topic is infrastructure cost and AI cost.

 - Press and practitioners quote us without being pitched.

 - Customers and partners ask to be part of the next campaign.


WHY POINTFIVE

 - Founders with a track record: Built and sold IntSights to Rapid7. Backed by top-tier investors with deep conviction in this category.

 - Category-defining product: DeepWaste detection and agentic remediation with clear, measurable ROI for both engineering and finance teams.

 - Early-stage leverage: Your work directly shapes the product, the culture, and the go-to-market playbook.

 - A category that is wide open for a distinctive voice.

 - Direct access to founders and leadership and room to ship without layers of approval.

 - Real budget for ideas that earn it, and credit for the work.
